I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the safest and most familiar way for me to make use of a full year in Quzhou County. I would not change to a risky cash crop at my age. Winter wheat fits our land and weather, and summer maize follows it well after harvest. I will use improved seed because I want steadier yield and better resistance, but I will keep management simple and practical. For wheat, I will focus on base fertilizer, one or two irrigations if water is tight, and a few pesticide sprays only when needed for aphids, rust, or other common problems. For maize, I will sow soon after wheat harvest, use a little more nitrogen, watch the field after emergence, and irrigate at the key growth stages if rainfall is short. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and cheaper for me to manage than deep ploughing every season, and it fits the wheat-maize system well. My goal is not the highest possible yield, but a stable harvest with work I can realistically handle.
